ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and ongoing screening of all directors, founding shareholders, and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) domestic targeted-financial-sanctions notices issued under s. 26B of FICA read together with the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any interest at or above the 5% statutory beneficial-ownership threshold, for all foreign and domestic Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) per FIC guidance, and for this Medium_Risk_Enhanced digital media arbitrage profile. EDD must capture source of funds and wealth, jurisdiction risk, media-network counterparty risk, and expected payment rail types (Mercury ACH, wire transfer, Wise) before bank onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) Electronic Name Reservation System, accessible at https://eservices.cipc.co.za (manual submission via Form CoR 9.1)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin script and in any of the 11 official languages of South Africa; a name of foreign origin must be transliterated or accompanied by a translation into English; the suffix '(Pty) Ltd' is statutorily required for private companies and cannot be localized or omitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name is valid for 180 days and is not extendable; if the name lapses, a fresh eName reservation must be submitted. Upon statutory refusal, the applicant may file Form CoR 30.1 (Application for Reconsideration of a Decision of the Commission) with CIPC within 20 business days of the refusal, attaching any required ministerial or sector-regulator approvals and two alternative name candidates; a further appeal lies to the Companies Tribunal under s. 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. If incorporation is completed within the reservation window, the reserved name converts into the registered name and loses its temporary character.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional - s. 23(3)(b) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 requires a physical street address in the Republic where statutory records are kept and legal process can be served; a pure mail-forwarding virtual address with no records custody is insufficient. A reputable serviced-office or co-working address providing a real street address, registered-agent presence, mail handling, and records access is acceptable for this license-free digital media-buying industry, provided the address is not a P.O. Box and is verifiable by CIPC, FIC, and SARS.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate - approximately 15-20% probability of an unannounced CIPC or FIC address verification, or a SARS site visit under s. 60 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, within the first operating year for a standard ISIC 7310 entity. The probability rises above 40% if the registered office is a mass-serviced virtual address flagged in FIC money-laundering risk mapping, if beneficial-ownership filings are delayed, or if the company is selected for CIPC annual compliance enforcement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, principally sections 13 (incorporation), 14 (registration of incorporation), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (legal personality and capacity), 66 (board) and 69 (disqualification of directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation in Form CoR 14.1, accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued share capital is prescribed for a private company (Pty) Ltd; the MOI must state authorised shares and the consideration for shares may be cash or an undertaking. CIPC does not require depot of paid-up capital in escrow; however, for bank account opening and immigration compliance, an equity injection of at least ZAR 10,000 is commonly evidenced, and exchange-control escrow rules apply only to inward-listed investment arrangements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the sole incorporator subscribes to 100 ordinary shares of no par value and adopts the Memorandum of Incorporation as filed. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office is fixed at the address recorded in the Notice of Incorporation, South Africa. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Full Name] is appointed sole director, and [Secretary Name], where required, is appointed company secretary, to hold office under the Companies Act 71 of 2008. RESOLVED FURTHER that the director is authorized to open bank accounts, execute CIPC and SARS filings, and appoint professional advisors for operational licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Memorandum of Incorporation Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form CoR 9.1 for name reservation online with up to three proposed names; if the name is not reserved, incorporate using the company registration number and amend the name later. Prepare the MOI on Form CoR 15.1A or a bespoke MOI, execute it before a commissioner of oaths, and verify name availability using the CIPC name checker.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1A or custom) signed before a commissioner of oaths
Identity document or passport of the incorporator
Tax identification number of the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the reserved name is refused, file a name-objection under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 or reserve an alternative name within five business days through the CIPC e-Services portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of Notice of Incorporation and MOI with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation), attach the executed MOI, registered office particulars, director consent forms, and pay the prescribed filing fee. Submit through the CIPC e-Services portal; the system will issue a company registration number and payment reference. Retain the electronic submission receipt and system-generated acknowledgement.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation signed by the incorporator
Director consent to act in Form CoR 6 or equivalent
Registered office physical and postal address details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a material defect query on the MOI, revise and resubmit the MOI through the e-Services portal within ten business days. Any defect in incorporation may be cured by a director or shareholder resolution and re-filing in accordance with section 14(5) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Registration Certificate and Corporate Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After CIPC approval, download the Registration Certificate, Notice of Registration, and Company Extract from the CIPC company documents portal. Verify the enterprise number, directors, registered address, and share structure against the MOI and CoR 14.1.
required_dossiers: Filing fee receipt or CIPC account confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the company extract contains inaccurate particulars, file Form CoR 28 (Change of Business Information) together with a supporting affidavit through the CIPC e-Services portal to correct the administrative record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Company Tax Registration and Tax Compliance Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Income Tax through SARS eFiling or Form IT77 to obtain an Income Tax Reference Number. A Tax Compliance Status Pin should be applied for, and VAT registration must be completed only if the company is required to register under section 23 of the VAT Act; voluntary registration may be appropriate for affiliate media-buying contracts in the ordinary course.
required_dossiers: Bank account confirmation or proof of initial share capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects the registration due to address or beneficial-ownership information, file an amended IT77 through an authorised representative and submit a physical address declaration with supporting lease or utility document to SARS branches.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL) / Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer for UIF and the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) if any employees are engaged. If the company commences with no employees, make a written declaration to that effect on the DEL portal to remain compliant and avoid late-registration penalties.
required_dossiers: ID or passport copies of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DEL portal merges duplicate employer records or delays the employer number, file an affidavit confirming the first date of engagement and request manual processing through the Provincial Labour Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning, Occupational Health and Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipality (e.g., City of Johannesburg Municipal Planning Department) and Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the zoning of the leased physical premises for general office or information technology services. Obtain a Certificate of Occupancy, verify compliance with the National Building Regulations, arrange a fire extinguisher and emergency-escape inspection, and complete a workplace risk assessment under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993. If the municipality requires a standard business registration or trading certificate, file that application before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of premises ownership
Municipal zoning certificate or town-planning approval
Workplace risk assessment and OHS plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality identifies a zoning non-compliance, file an application for a use-right or building-plan amendment under the Spatial Planning and Land Use Management Act 16 of 2013, or relocate to compliant premises and submit an amended registered address to CIPC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial licensing authority applies to affiliate media buying; for physical premises the competent authorities are the local municipality and the Department of Employment and Labour.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industry-specific operating or manufacturing permit is required for a digital advertising and media-buying company; a municipal premises or occupational-health certificate is only applicable if a physical office is established.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - administrative information-technology office use does not trigger a listed activity under the 2014 EIA Regulations, Listing Notices 1, 2 or 3; no Environmental Authorisation is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater effluent or VOC emission threshold applies. E-waste generated by media-buying operations must be disposed of in accordance with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008, and general solid waste limits imposed by the responsible municipality apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety must comply with the National Building Regulations and SANS 10400, including fire-extinguisher inspection, emergency escape routes, and occupancy load certification. A structural load clearance is required for rooms containing heavy server racks or computing equipment exceeding 150 kg/m2, and an OHS plan with an appointed safety officer is required under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – www.sarsefiling.co.za; eFiling platform
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd must first incorporate via the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) to obtain an enterprise registration number. Thereafter, the company applies to SARS for an Income Tax Reference Number by completing the SARS registration application via eFiling or a SARS branch, providing the CIPC registration certificate, memorandum of incorporation, certified identity documents or passports of directors/shareholders, and proof of registered and principal place of business in South Africa. For VAT, the company registers as a VAT vendor where the value of taxable supplies exceeds or is expected to exceed R1,000,000 within any consecutive 12-month period, or voluntarily where the threshold is met as a foreign non-resident supplier supplying electronic services in South Africa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under South African law. South African companies are taxed on worldwide income, with special rules for foreign business establishments. Hybrid mismatch provisions under Section 8F to 8L of the Income Tax Act apply to prevent deduction/non-inclusion mismatches, but no elective classification regimes analogous to the US are available. Certain companies can elect the deemed corporate income tax incidence under the 'nil return' system, but this is not a substantive classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) – administered under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 (ZAR) in annual taxable supplies, measured over any 12-month rolling period; compulsory for residents and foreign businesses supplying electronic services to South African residents, unless solely making exempt supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate real-time tax clearance or digital stamping for standard B2B invoices. SARS supports voluntary e-invoicing and interoperable electronic data interchange, but all invoices must contain prescribed particulars under VAT Act Section 20. Tax clearance certificates are issued through eFiling, and real-time electronic submissions are required for VAT returns and customs declarations. No API-based fiscal stamping or continuous transaction controls are currently imposed for standard VAT invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from South Africa are zero-rated under Section 11 of the VAT Act where the supplier retains documentary proof of export and the goods physically leave the country within the prescribed period. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated where the services are exported in the sense that they are not supplied to a resident, are not connected to movable or immovable property in South Africa, and are deemed to be supplied outside South Africa under Section 11(2)(l). Sales of goods and services to registered vendors in the BLNS countries (Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia, Eswatini) are zero-rated only where the buyer is a registered VAT vendor and the goods are removed from South Africa under covered cross-border arrangements, subject to strict documentary proof.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SA Customs SAD500) reflecting correct tariff code and final export destination
Bill of Lading or air waybill showing consignor and consignee names, port of loading, and port of discharge
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank foreign exchange confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds in South Africa
Proof of physical movement such as a border crossing receipt, transport manifest, or terminal export certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may disallow zero-rating and impose a VAT assessment with understatement penalties from 10% to 150% where a person knowingly or negligently makes a false declaration or fails to retain prescribed documentation. Fraudulent export claims attract criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act, including fines up to R100,000 or imprisonment, and can trigger voluntary disclosure penalties and retrospective clawbacks of all refunds, interest at the prescribed rate, and additional 200% penalties for intentional tax evasion. Exchange Control Regulation R.21 requires export proceeds to be received in South Africa within 180 days; contraventions are referred to the Financial Surveillance Department and may result in administrative penalties and denial of future zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Exchange Control Regulations and the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is fully convertible for current account transactions including legitimate payments for services such as digital advertising and media buying, provided supporting documents are presented to and approved by an authorised dealer. Capital account transactions are restricted; direct inward foreign investment into a South African (Pty) Ltd is freely permitted via a share subscription but all proceeds must be credited to a South African bank account with a share certificate and beneficial ownership declaration filed. Dividends and profits may be remitted abroad by non-resident shareholders on a current account basis through an authorised dealer, subject to evidence of tax compliance (SARS tax clearance for dividends), an IMD (International Money-Dividend) declaration, and no adverse exchange-control findings. There are no dual exchange rates or surrender requirements on retained foreign currency, but all export receipts must be converted to ZAR into the local operational account. Remuneration for offshore marketing services is considered an invisible export and is therefore current-account eligible if properly documented and accurately priced at arm's length.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For services exports by an advertising and media-buying company, the service provider must receive payment of export proceeds within 180 days of date of invoice or date of service completion, whichever is earlier. Upon receipt in the authorised dealer's foreign currency account, the proceeds must be surrendered into a ZAR-denominated account of the (Pty) Ltd within 30 days of receipt, unless a specific retention facility has been granted by SARB FinSurv. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio requiring 100% conversion for service exports; however, 100% of proceeds are generally required to be remitted to South Africa and credited to the authorised dealer in either foreign currency or ZAR, with only limited retention allowed for working capital or approved offshore disbursements. All export proceeds must be accompanied by an export/bank transaction number, a valid service contract or invoice, and a proof of payment from the overseas client; no third-party settlement is permitted unless explicitly authorised by FinSurv. For digital advertising arbitrage, the intermediary service is zero-rated for VAT purposes when sold to a non-resident, and the SARB treats such revenues as current account receipts requiring no prior exchange control approval, but the bank will still require auditable evidence of the underlying performance media transactions to distinguish true sales from round-tripping.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech and EMI platforms such as Mercury, Wise, and Payoneer have low-to-medium viability as the primary treasury rail for a South African corporate entity because they do not hold a South African banking licence and are not authorised dealers in foreign exchange. Such platforms can be used as ancillary payment concentrators for the receipt of advertising proceeds from international DSPs, but all funds eventually must be routed to a local bank account in the name of the Pty Ltd to satisfy SARB export proceeds surrender obligations. Wise Business may be deactivated if the South African entity's turnover exceeds exchange-control thresholds without a local bank backing. As a practical alternative, an institutional-grade solution is to use the South African branch of an international bank (e.g., Citibank or HSBC) paired with a local tier-1 bank; this arrangement offers SWIFT-based cross-border liquidity without violating the SARB authorised-dealer requirement. The compliance ceiling is that all offshore digital EMI transactions are treated as repayments, loans, or trade payments from a non-resident source; the South African entity must, without exception, maintain and export an audit trail from the EMI to the local authorised-dealer bank showing underlying client contracts, campaign invoices, and conversion evidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under South Africa's Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA), every bank must conduct risk-based customer due diligence. For a non-resident-owned (Pty) Ltd in the digital advertising sector, a physical appearance of at least one director is highly recommended but not always strictly mandatory if the bank offers remote electronic identity verification with FICA-compliant video calls, biometric matching, and notarised director documents. In practice, tier-1 banks will require either (i) an in-branch interview with at least one natural-person director, or (ii) a local South African representative who holds power of attorney and can attend the bank in person for the verification act. Remote-only onboarding is possible only for certain account types if the beneficial owner is from a low-risk jurisdiction and the company can provide apostilled/certified copies of the memorandum of incorporation, director ID, proof of residential address, and the foreign parent's corporate register. The high-risk sector profile (performance-based media buying involves many counterparties, rapid fund flows, and potential affiliate fraud) triggers enhanced due diligence and the firm should expect a request for an in-person or virtual compliance interview with the bank's Financial Crime Risk division, particularly to explain the affiliate network flow, the commercial reasonableness of margins, and the source of funds for the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership residing in an OFAC / FATF monitoring jurisdiction or a jurisdiction with high money-laundering risk, creating ambiguity on ultimate economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Delivery of an organisational chart showing the direct and indirect beneficial owners, notarised certificates of incorporation of all intermediate entities, official register excerpts from the corporate registry, passports of senior management, and a signed declaration identifying each ultimate natural person. The dossier should include a reputable independent corporate-service provider (TCSP) cover opinion and, where applicable, a foreign tax residence certificate to demonstrate economic nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or inflated 'media buying' activity generating rapid round-tripping of funds between the affiliate company and affiliated merchants.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A granular business dossier containing executed advertising insertion orders, programmatic DSP contracts, ad-serving platform logs, screenshot of conversion attestations (tracking IDs, click IDs, conversion timestamps), settlement statements from affiliate networks, and an expert explanation of EBITDA margins. Evidence must show that the revenue is not self-referral or fraudulent click arbitrage; a third-party forensic audit of campaign delivery metrics and a traceable chain of funds from ad networks to the company bank account is required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionately high foreign revenue for a newly incorporated entity with low initial staff, triggering shell company suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A fully substantiated operational substance file: lease or serviced-office agreement in South Africa, FICA-verified employee contracts, payroll records, invoice reconciliation showing the exact campaign periods, access logs from media-buying dashboards, and an interconnected telecom/IT invoice trail. The company must demonstrate that the marketing decision-making, creative selection, budget setting, and campaign optimisation professionals operate in South Africa, not merely the invoicing entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sample/total amount of source-of-funds request for the inward capital injection cannot be matched against credible wealth accumulation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A bank reference from the parent company's home jurisdiction, signed audited financial statements of the parent, source-of-funds evidence (e.g., 12 months of bank statements, share sale agreements, dividend vouchers), plus the share subscription agreement and the SARB prescribed Authorised Dealer Form. If the parent is newly funded by private lenders, a legally executed loan agreement, lender due-diligence file, and evidence of loan transfer from the lending institution directly to the South African company's capital account are required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound foreign direct investment for the South African Pty Ltd's working capital or share capital must be paid from the foreign shareholder's bank account to a dedicated ZAR capital account at a SARB authorised dealer. The wire must be SWIFT MT103 containing the correct corporate beneficiary name, legal entity identifier where available, and a clear narrative such as 'Share Subscription' or 'Direct Investment' with the authorised dealer's exchange control reference. The receiving bank must issue a 'Form ADF' declaration of inward transfers; the transaction will be classified under direct investment and credited to a 'suspense/escrow' account if needed. The company must submit a share certificate within 30 days, together with the inward transfer advice and a beneficial-ownership declaration, to enable the authorised dealer to report to SARB FinSurv. Once the share certificate is issued, funds may be transferred from the suspense account to the operational account. Alternatively, structured external borrowings (intragroup loans) require a loan/equity ratio approved by the authorised dealer under the Currency and Exchanges Manual, with formal letters of support and registration of all external debt. The same MT103 should not be used for mixed equity and trade settlement; separate purpose codes are required to avoid exchange-control reconciliation errors.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments to non-resident suppliers, DSPs, affiliate networks, and advertising publishers are current-account transactions and can be executed by the authorised dealer via SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) or SWIFT MT202 (bank transfer) at the instruction of the corporate account holder. For trade-related services, banks may require a trade IBAN or bank details of the beneficiary, but the critical compliance step is the submission of pro-forma invoices or early settlement invoices proving that the payment is directly for the admitted marketing services and is not a disguised capital outflow. When purchasing media inventory or paying advertising publishers abroad, the company should use its operational account with the instruction narrative 'Cross-border media placement settlement', attaching campaign media plan and publisher statement. Commercial letters of credit (documentary L/C) are less common for serially repeated media buying but are appropriate for large-scale performance campaigns or when contracting a foreign holding company. On the condition that the payment is denominated in EUR/USD/GBP or another freely convertible currency, the authorised dealer will debit the ZAR account and execute a spot conversion at the prevailing market rate, or use an existing forward contract. For retained foreign-currency export proceeds, the company may instruct the dealer to disburse directly to third-party foreign suppliers using an ISD (Inward/Outward transfer) instruction; in that case a 'reservation of foreign currency' authorisation and an audited trail of the original export proceeds are mandatory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) for firm commitments to purchase or sell foreign currency within a maximum period of 12 months, renewable with proof of an underlying current-account transaction
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on ZAR/USD or ZAR/EUR where permitted by the authorised dealer, subject to underlying exposure and SARB restrictions on speculative trading
Cross-currency swap for converting fixed or floating-rate debt from ZAR to foreign currency, strictly matched to underlying external loan commitments
Vanilla currency option (put/call) purchased from an authorised dealer for hedging forecast advertising revenues, provided the option is clearly trade-structure-based and not speculative
Spot-Futures margin hedges offered by licensed domestic brokers on safex, aligned with actual cash flow exposure under the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act (FAIS)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (CIPC Form AR) incl. beneficial ownership confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fees accrue immediately after the deadline; CIPC issues a compliance notice; persistent non-filing for two consecutive financial years triggers Section 82 deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register and annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the CIPC Annual Return; within 10 business days of any shareholding change or UBO update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to ZAR 1 million per contravention; directors may be disqualified; repeated non-compliance may lead to deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (IFRS / IFRS-for-SMEs) and audit/review report (if PIS threshold met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (only when the company is required to be audited or reviewed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS to be prepared within 6 months after financial year-end; filed with CIPC within 30 business days after board approval if audited/reviewed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with Sections 30 and 33 constitutes an offence; CIPC compliance notice followed by administrative penalties; directors liable for default

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more; independent review required if PIS is between 100 and 349; no audit/review required if PIS is below 100 unless the MOI requires otherwise. PIS is calculated from turnover, employees, third-party liabilities and shareholder count.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS as issued by the IASB); IFRS for SMEs is permitted for companies without public accountability and with PIS below 350.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a register of beneficial owners and confirm its accuracy on each annual return. Any transfer of shares, change in control or in UBO details requires an updated beneficial ownership filing with CIPC within 10 business days. The register must be open to inspection by CIPC and SARS.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 12,000 per annum (only if PIS ≥ 350)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad statutory tax holiday exists in South Africa. Selective incentives include the Section 11D research and development allowance (additional deduction), the Employment Tax Incentive for qualifying employees, and the Small Business Corporation progressive tax regime (0%-21%) for companies meeting turnover and shareholder requirements. Assessed trading losses are carried forward indefinitely, subject to an 80% annual utilisation cap, with no sunset period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SARS ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return), filed electronically through SARS eFiling or a registered tax practitioner’s portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the end of the company’s financial year. Provisional tax payments are rendered semiannually under the IRP6 regime: the first estimate is due within six months of the start of the tax year; the second estimate (top-up) is due before or on the last business day of the tax year; the final balancing payment is reconciled with the ITR14.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax reference number, company registration number, financial year-end, registered and postal address, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the South African income tax reference number issued to the Pty Ltd entity. A company incorporated in South Africa is taxed as a full resident taxpayer; non-resident status applies only to the shareholders, not to the company’s return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income, exempt income, general and specific deductions, allowances, assessed loss offsets, and net taxable income calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all media-buying commissions, affiliate lead-gen fees, volume rebates, arbitrage mark-ups, and foreign-source receipts. Deductions must satisfy the 'wholly and exclusively' requirement and be substantiated by documentary evidence such as media purchase invoices and traffic partner proof.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section 3 - Capital Gains and Losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disposal of capital assets, determination of proceeds, base cost, capital loss, annual exclusion, inclusion rate, and corporate capital gains tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where intangible digital assets or foreign shareholdings are disposed of, apply the 80% capital gain inclusion rate and a 21.6% effective corporate tax rate on the net gain. A foreign tax credit may reduce this if foreign capital gains tax is paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section 4 - Tax Calculation and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 27% corporate tax rate, rebates, foreign tax credits, provisional tax credits, and total annual tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding taxes on advertising revenue or overseas interest must be claimed through the foreign tax credit mechanism. Supporting OECD tax certificates and Schedule I calculations are required for credit reduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section 5 - Related-Party and Transfer Pricing Disclosures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of shareholding structure, connected persons, cross-border related-party transactions, and transfer pricing policies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Full contemporaneous disclosures are required where trade or financial transactions with foreign related parties exceed administrative thresholds. Attach a Local File and, where applicable, a Master File and CbC Report under sections 31, 25A and the Tax Administration Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late ITR14 filing triggers an administrative non-compliance penalty under section 210 of the Tax Administration Act (up to ZAR 16,000 per month), an estimated assessment under section 95, a 10% late-payment penalty, and prescribed interest. A deliberate understatement or non-filing may attract a section 223 understatement penalty of 10% to 100% of the additional tax.
